principles: Completeness is mechanically derived, never self-reported.
One canonical owner per fact and no parallel writable acceptance truth.
Unsupported knowledge and disagreement fail closed.
Every consumed claim is issuer-, digest-, workspace- and freshness-bound.
drivers: Wave 2 and Wave 3 need replayable basis identities without recomputing against a different workspace.
Reviewers need deterministic diagnostics and omission/tamper bites.
Proofbound already has signed process-fact and canonical freshness infrastructure.
Discovery support must be explicit per language/profile.

options.name: A: Verifier-issued durable signed receipt with recomputable adapter inputs
pros: Replayable exact basis identity for later gates
Clear legal writer and signature verification
Can bind adapter-result digests and current workspace/scope hashes
cons: Requires careful stale classification and atomic writes

options.name: B: Recomputable basis section inside proofstory.json
cons: Mixes caller-authored topology envelope with verifier-owned inventory
Harder to prove writer separation and replay the exact prior PLAN basis

options.name: C: Pure read-time report with no signed receipt
cons: Cannot safely bind later Wave 2/3 consumers
No stable replay or omission-proof receipt

chosen: A: Verifier-issued durable signed receipt with recomputable adapter inputs
rationale: Choose A because later structural and pre-review gates require a stable, independently issued basis identity. The receipt is generated only by the registered verifier, while the underlying adapter results remain reproducible and digest-bound. This preserves ProofStory topology as reference-only and prevents a second caller-writable truth source.

preMortem.scenario: Caller injects an inventory and forces complete
preMortem.trigger: CLI or normalization accepts paths/status fields from request payload
preMortem.consequence: False completeness can satisfy later gates
preMortem.mitigation: Command schema accepts only story/profile selection; handler recomputes every path and status, with mutation tests rejecting write-shaped payloads.

preMortem.trigger: Registry/config changes but receipt generation does not require the adapter set
preMortem.consequence: Coverage shrinks while status remains complete
preMortem.mitigation: Versioned adapter policy declares required IDs; receipt binds policy and result digests; omission mutation must yield partial.

preMortem.trigger: One adapter observes a handler/consumer absent from another
preMortem.consequence: A path is silently lost or duplicated
preMortem.mitigation: Union all paths, emit deterministic disagreement diagnostics, and classify partial until explicitly reconciled.

preMortem.scenario: Old receipt is rebound to a new hash
preMortem.trigger: Metadata-only writer changes head/workspace fields without rerunning adapters
preMortem.mitigation: Sign semantic fields plus adapter outputs and canonical scope/story/closure hashes; legal writer always executes verifier and rejects hash-only rebind.

preMortem.scenario: Topology or reviewer prose authors completeness
preMortem.trigger: Basis verifier trusts acceptanceTopology refs or evidence notes as discovered paths
preMortem.mitigation: Topology is only compared after independent discovery; prose is never parsed as protocol; tests delete topology rows while basis remains and vice versa.

preMortem.scenario: Unsupported language is treated as empty complete
preMortem.trigger: No matching adapter returns an empty result without unsupported classification
preMortem.mitigation: Profiles without a sufficient registered adapter set return unsupported, never complete.
